b: Social Media Wins with mdg is a contributed article from Sara Fellows, Group Director, Communications at mdg.

CHICAGO — At mdg, we’re challenging the idea that social media is simply a promotional channel for events. From turning influencers into an extension of the show floor to bringing pop culture into highly specialized industries, we’re finding new ways to build communities, create connections and drive measurable results. Here’s what that looks like in action.
SUPERZOO: Turning Influencers into Part of the Event Experience
What if influencers weren’t just invited to cover an event, but were actually part of the experience?

For SUPERZOO 2026, we took influencer marketing beyond sponsored posts and built a program designed to bring creators, exhibitors and the broader pet industry together. Through a curated credentialing program, intentional creator outreach and a dedicated Creator Crawl, we created opportunities for influencers to discover products, connect directly with brands and share their experiences with their communities.
The result was more than event coverage. We helped turn the show floor into a content engine, extending the SUPERZOO experience to millions of people who weren’t physically there.
International Baking Industry Exposition (IBIE): Building a Social Strategy that Keeps an Industry Engaged Year-Round
How do you keep an audience engaged when your event only happens once every three years?

For IBIE 2025, we started by listening. We conducted industry research to understand what baking professionals were talking about, the challenges they were facing and the topics that mattered most to them. Those insights became the foundation of a new social media strategy, complete with defined content pillars that guided every single post.

Instead of relying on promotional messaging, we built a content engine around the industry’s interests, from education and innovation to the people and trends shaping the future of baking. Every post had a purpose, and every piece of content connected back to our strategy.

The result? Significant improvements in social performance and an engaged community that continues to connect with the event, even during its three-year show cycle. It’s proof that when you give people a reason to follow you beyond registration, social media can become a year-round destination for your industry.
+51% growth in followers compared to the 2022 campaign
+215% increase in total engagements compared to 2022
7.38% average engagement rate across the 2025 campaign
Society of Breast Imaging: Bringing Pop Culture into a Highly Specialized Industry
Who says a professional medical association can’t participate in pop culture?

“For the Society of Breast Imaging, we’ve been rethinking how to make highly technical, educational content feel more relatable and engaging on social media. By combining expert-led educational series with relevant trends, humor and cultural moments, we’re meeting breast imaging professionals where they are, without compromising the credibility of the association.

It’s a great example of why understanding your audience’s pop culture DNA matters. Sometimes the most effective way to connect with a highly specialized professional audience is to remember they’re people first.

More than 13,000 views from a single trend-driven Instagram post
